To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 5′ region of R2 RNA controls the R2 protein's binding to DNA, and that this RNA is required for the second strand cleavage step in R2 retrotranscription.
the R2 protein has two distinct DNA-binding conformations and that the R2 5′ RNA controls which conformation the protein assumes.
RNA sequences from near the 3′ and 5′ end regulate the DNA binding and cleavage activities of R2 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which the R2 retroelement inserts into the genome of the host cell.
the mechanisms by which retroviruses and retrotransposons replicate and insert into genomes of higher eukaryotes.
the mechanism of R2 retrotransposable element replication, which occurs by a target primed reverse transcription ( TPRT ) mechanism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNA from the 5' end of the R1 retrotransposon is required for the protein to cleave the second strand of its DNA target.
the 5′-end RNA sequence of the R2 RNA controls the R2 protein's binding to DNA and its cleavage of DNA.
the RNA from the 5 ′ end of the R 2 retrotransposons controls R 2 protein binding to its DNA target site and cleaves its DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the R2 protein is a DNA nuclease, and that the RNA from the 5’ end of the R1/R2 element is a regulator of the R2 DNA nuclease activity.
the RNA from the 5' end of the R1 element is the critical determinant for the R1 protein to bind to the downstream DNA sequences.

RNA can regulate protein-DNA binding and that RNA can be used in a temporal fashion to regulate a biochemical process.
